units.sourceHTML:
This creates a new variable ⟦CODE0⟧ in the current scope and initializes it with
the result of the expression following the ⟦CODE1⟧. Once a variable has been
defined, it can be accessed by name as you would expect.
units.originalInnerHTML: This creates a new variable a in the current scope and initializes it with the result of the expression following the =. Once a variable has been defined, it can be accessed by name as you would expect.

units.sourceHTML: Wren has true block scope: a variable exists from the point where it is defined until the end of the block where that definition appears.
units.originalInnerHTML: Wren has true block scope: a variable exists from the point where it is defined until the end of the block where that definition appears.

units.sourceHTML: Variables defined at the top level of a script are top-level and are visible to the module system. All other variables are local. Declaring a variable in an inner scope with the same name as an outer one is called shadowing and is not an error (although it’s not something you likely intend to do much).
units.originalInnerHTML: Variables defined at the top level of a script are top-level and are visible to the module system. All other variables are local. Declaring a variable in an inner scope with the same name as an outer one is called shadowing and is not an error (although it’s not something you likely intend to do much).

units.sourceHTML: Declaring a variable with the same name in the same scope is an error.
units.originalInnerHTML: Declaring a variable with the same name in the same scope is an error.

units.sourceHTML: After a variable has been declared, you can assign to it using ⟦CODE0⟧
units.originalInnerHTML: After a variable has been declared, you can assign to it using =

units.sourceHTML:
An assignment walks up the scope stack to find where the named variable is
declared. It’s an error to assign to a variable that isn’t defined. Wren
doesn’t roll with implicit variable definition.
units.originalInnerHTML:
An assignment walks up the scope stack to find where the named variable is
declared. It’s an error to assign to a variable that isn’t defined. Wren
doesn’t roll with implicit variable definition.

units.sourceHTML:
When used in a larger expression, an assignment expression evaluates to the
assigned value.
units.originalInnerHTML:
When used in a larger expression, an assignment expression evaluates to the
assigned value.

units.sourceHTML: If the left-hand side is some more complex expression than a bare variable name, then it isn’t an assignment. Instead, it’s calling a setter method.
units.originalInnerHTML: If the left-hand side is some more complex expression than a bare variable name, then it isn’t an assignment. Instead, it’s calling a setter method.
